description: District Energy in Cities is a 2015 report of the United Nations Environment Programme on modern district heating and cooling. The abstract in the UNEP knowledge repository, read on 2026-09-26, says it is among the first publications to give concrete policy, finance and technology best practice guidance on the heating and cooling sectors in cities through energy efficiency and renewable integration, and the first to consolidate data on the multiple benefits that cities, countries and regions have achieved with modern district energy. Coverage is global, drawn from city case studies. The format is a single English PDF of 14.1 MB, downloadable at no cost from the repository's communication materials collection; the page states no licence. Caveats: the data are from 2015 or earlier and are presented in report tables and case texts, not as a machine-readable data set, so values must be extracted by hand and checked against newer sources. Simulation uses are benchmark costs, benefits and policy settings for capacity planning of district energy schemes and for climate adaptation and mitigation planning in cities. Related records: data-heat-roadmap-europe-peta4 maps heat demand and district heating potential, and data-eu27-district-heating-potentials estimates potentials across the EU.
